The first reaction is a Michael addition of 2-ethyl-2,6-dimethylcyclohexan-1-one to ethyl acrylate using t-BuOK. The ketone has alpha-hydrogens only at C6 (C2 is fully substituted). The bulky base deprotonates C6, forming an enolate that attacks the β-carbon of ethyl acrylate. The product is 2-ethyl-2,6-dimethyl-6-(3-ethoxy-3-oxopropyl)cyclohexan-1-one. Renumbering the ring with the propanoate attachment as C1 gives the systematic name ethyl 3-(3-ethyl-1,3-dimethyl-2-oxocyclohexyl)propanoate.

The second reaction is a Michael addition of the nitronate from 1-nitropropane (deprotonated by KOH) to (E)-but-2-enenitrile. The nitronate attacks the β-carbon (C3) of the α,β-unsaturated nitrile, followed by protonation with water. The product is CH₃CH₂CH(NO₂)CH(CH₃)CH₂CN, which is named 3-methyl-4-nitrohexanenitrile.

Both products match option (D).

Answer: D
